title: Sail Switch Not Closing
shortDescription: The airflow sail switch isn't detecting blower airflow to permit ignition.
fullDescription:
Suburban RV furnaces use a sail switch — a paddle in the blower housing — to prove airflow before gas valve opens. If the switch doesn't close within ~30 seconds of blower start, the furnace locks out.

Causes: obstructed duct, failing blower motor, dirty/rusty sail switch contacts, or rodent nest in ductwork.

Sail switch is a safety — don't bypass. Without proven airflow, the heat exchanger can overheat.

causes.cause: Blocked return air or supply ducts

fixSteps.title: Clear ducts
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect return air grille and supply registers for blockage.

fixSteps.title: Check blower speed
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm blower at full RPM — no bearing noise.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sail switch
fixSteps.instruction: Remove furnace access, verify paddle moves freely, clean contacts.

whenToCallPro: If blower motor needs replacement or ductwork is sealed behind cabinetry.
videoSearchQuery: Suburban RV furnace sail switch fix

faq.q: Can I bend the sail to make it trigger easier?
faq.a: Don't — that defeats the safety; clean the switch instead.

title: High Limit Switch Tripped
shortDescription: Heat exchanger temperature exceeded safe limit and shut down the furnace.
fullDescription:
The high-limit switch on Suburban furnaces opens around 200°F to protect the heat exchanger from overfiring. Repeated tripping indicates poor airflow, oversized orifice, or blocked heat exchanger.

It's typically an auto-reset switch — the furnace retries after cooldown. If it trips again quickly, do not keep resetting.

Running past a chronic limit trip can crack the heat exchanger — allowing CO into the cabin.

causes.cause: Weak blower not moving enough air

symptoms: Furnace fires, gets hot, then shuts off

fixSteps.title: Open all registers
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure at least 75% of supply vents are open.

fixSteps.title: Inspect heat exchanger
fixSteps.instruction: Remove exterior vent and look for debris/nesting.

fixSteps.title: Test limit switch
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity cold — should be closed.

whenToCallPro: If heat exchanger may be cracked — CO risk requires professional inspection.
videoSearchQuery: Suburban RV furnace high limit trip

faq.q: How many registers should I have open?
faq.a: At least 3/4 of them — restricted airflow is the #1 cause of limit trips.

title: Gas Valve Fails To Open
shortDescription: The 12V gas valve solenoid is not opening on ignition call.
fullDescription:
Suburban furnaces use a redundant dual-coil gas valve. Both coils must energize for gas to flow. A single coil fault disables the whole valve.

Measure valve coil resistance (should be 40-90 ohms per coil) and voltage during call for heat (should see 12V).

Soap-test all gas joints after replacement — any leak is a fire hazard.
symptoms: Blower runs, spark clicks, no flame

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off propane, swap valve, leak test.

whenToCallPro: If you can't leak-check with soap solution — any propane leak is a life-safety issue.
videoSearchQuery: Suburban RV furnace gas valve replace

faq.q: Are Suburban and Atwood valves interchangeable?

title: Blower Motor Fault / Low RPM
shortDescription: The blower motor has seized, lost bearings, or is running below threshold RPM.
fullDescription:
Suburban furnaces use a single motor with two squirrel-cage fans (combustion + circulation). Bearing wear causes growl and slow spin-up; seized motor = no ignition.

Unless you have an exact OEM motor replacement, replace the motor as a complete assembly with mounting hardware.

High-current motor can ignite flammable debris if armature burns — clear nesting material before retry.

fixSteps.title: Check battery voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Motor needs at least 11.5V under load.

whenToCallPro: If the furnace is built into a difficult cabinet location — removal can require cutting access panels.
videoSearchQuery: Suburban RV furnace blower motor replace

faq.a: Most Suburban motors are sealed — replacement is the standard fix.

title: Direct Spark Ignition Lockout
shortDescription: Three ignition trials failed, furnace locked out.
fullDescription:
Suburban DSI modules spark for ~7 seconds, sense flame rectification, and retry up to 3 times. Lockout after 3 fails — usually dirty burner, worn electrode, or low propane.

Reset by turning thermostat off for 30 seconds, then calling for heat again.

Don't keep resetting without diagnosis — propane enters the heat exchanger on each trial.
whenToCallPro: If DSI module replacement is needed — involves disassembly of control area.

faq.a: Insects nest in warm burner tubes over summer.

title: Blower Time Delay Relay Fault
shortDescription: The post-purge timer isn't functioning, causing short-cycle or no cool-down.
fullDescription:
The time-delay relay keeps the blower running 45-60 seconds after the burner shuts off, protecting the heat exchanger by purging combustion heat. A failed relay either stops the blower instantly or runs it continuously.

Replace the timer board — it's a simple plug-in module on most Suburban furnaces.
symptoms: Blower stops immediately when thermostat satisfied

fixSteps.title: Inspect relay
fixSteps.instruction: Verify connector seated, no burn marks.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed — this is a straightforward swap.
videoSearchQuery: Suburban RV furnace time delay relay

faq.q: Can I short the relay to bypass?
faq.a: No — bypassing the delay stresses the heat exchanger.

title: No Call For Heat From Thermostat
shortDescription: The wall thermostat isn't signaling the furnace despite being set.
fullDescription:
RV thermostats send 12V (or close a dry contact) to signal heat demand. If the furnace doesn't run at all — no blower, no light — the issue is often the thermostat, its batteries, or the wall wiring.

Jumper the W and R terminals at the thermostat plate to test if the furnace fires — bypasses the thermostat logic.

fixSteps.title: Check batteries and setpoint
fixSteps.instruction: Replace AAA batteries, set thermostat 5°F above room temp.

fixSteps.title: Jumper test
fixSteps.instruction: Remove thermostat, short W to R — if furnace fires, thermostat is bad.

whenToCallPro: If wall wiring fault — may involve pulling trim.
videoSearchQuery: Suburban RV furnace no call for heat

faq.a: Many yes — match voltage (12V) and terminal count.

title: Propane Odor Detected
shortDescription: Strong propane smell at or inside the RV during furnace operation.
fullDescription:
Propane odor during furnace operation is an emergency. Possible causes: leak at gas valve, cracked line inside coach, failed gas valve seat allowing continuous bleed, or incomplete combustion venting back.

Shut off propane at the tank immediately, ventilate the RV, and do not operate any electrical devices (including light switches).

Do NOT attempt to locate the leak with a flame — use soap solution or an electronic sniffer.

causes.cause: Loose fitting at furnace gas inlet

fixSteps.title: Close propane
fixSteps.instruction: Shut main tank valve, ventilate RV fully.

fixSteps.title: Leak test
fixSteps.instruction: With LP pressurized but furnace off, spray soap on all fittings.

fixSteps.title: Professional repair
fixSteps.instruction: Any unresolved leak requires RV tech.

whenToCallPro: Always if leak cannot be identified and tightened — propane leaks cause RV fires.

faq.q: Is slight gas odor normal at startup?
faq.a: Brief odor during DSI trial can be normal; persistent odor is not.

title: Furnace Short-Cycles
shortDescription: Furnace fires briefly then shuts off repeatedly without reaching setpoint.
fullDescription:
Short cycling — firing for 30-90 seconds then shutting down — usually indicates the high limit is close to tripping. Root causes: closed supply vents, oversized furnace for space, or thermostat poorly located (over a supply register).

Long-term short cycling wears out the ignition module and heat exchanger.

fixSteps.title: Check thermostat location
fixSteps.instruction: If in direct airflow, relocate or add deflector.

whenToCallPro: If limit keeps tripping with all vents open — heat exchanger may be compromised.

faq.q: How long should a normal cycle be?
faq.a: Usually 5-15 minutes of burner run time before satisfying thermostat.

title: Blower Runs But Only Cool Air
shortDescription: Furnace blower runs but burner never ignites.
fullDescription:
If the blower runs continuously and only cool air comes from the vents, the thermostat is asking for fan (green wire) but either the furnace isn't getting heat call (white) or DSI is in lockout.

Most RV thermostats don't have a separate fan mode for furnaces — if blower runs continuously without heat call, check for a wiring error at the thermostat plate.

causes.cause: Thermostat wired to W+G instead of W only

fixSteps.title: Check thermostat wiring
fixSteps.instruction: RV thermostats typically need only R and W for furnace only.

fixSteps.title: Reset DSI
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle thermostat off 30 sec and retry heat call.

whenToCallPro: If DSI lockout persists after cleaning burner.
videoSearchQuery: RV furnace blower runs no heat

faq.q: Can I run fan only mode?
faq.a: Most RV furnaces don't support fan-only — blower starts with heat call.
